processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The three steels were vacuum cast.
Annealed for 1 h at the temperature indicated in Table 1; Table 1 lists 1060 °C for the 2.5 Al alloy, giving approx. 140 μm coarse grain size.

processing_steps.method: uniaxial compression (specimen preparation for SFE TEM)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 12.7 mm diameter cylinders with axes parallel to the rolling direction were compressed to 5% true strain to introduce dislocations; slices sectioned at 45° from the compression axis for TEM.

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic, coarse-grained single-phase microstructure; austenite retained to room temperature by Ni and Cr alloying (not by carbon partitioning).

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dissociation of perfect dislocations into partial dislocations bounding a stacking fault
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Dissociated dislocations in {111} planes imaged by weak-beam dark-field TEM; the partial dislocation separation d increases with perfect dislocation character angle α. For the 2.5 Al alloy the partial separation is the lowest of the three alloys at a given angle, consistent with its highest SFE.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Dislocations gliding on {111} planes; grains with {111} planes nearly aligned with the foil plane were selected because they had favorable slip conditions during compression.
interfaces.interface_notes: Single-phase austenite; the only 'interfaces' are stacking faults between partial dislocations (no phase boundaries).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: 12.7 mm diameter cylinders with axes parallel to the rolling direction, compressed to 5% true strain; thin slices sectioned at 45° from the compression axis and electropolished with 95% acetic acid + 5% perchloric acid
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: SFE derived from partial dislocation separation (d) and character angle (α) via Eq. (1), using isotropic G = 74 GPa and ν = 0.3 and the experimental lattice parameter a0

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: seven coupons per alloy ground to a 600 grit finish and chemically polished 20 min in 10 parts water + 10 parts hydrogen peroxide + 1 part hydrofluoric acid
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: XRD with Cu Kα (λ = 0.154060 nm); a0 from linear regression of a0 vs cos²θ/sinθ extrapolated to θ = 90°; lowest and highest a0 discarded and the remaining five averaged

lattice_parameter.note: The absolute austenite lattice parameter of the 2.5 Al alloy is not printed numerically (Figure 2 shows it near 0.36 nm).

relative_lattice_parameter_change.note: 2.5 wt.% Al increases the austenite lattice parameter by 1.41 × 10^-3 nm relative to the base alloy.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Phillips X'Pert diffractometer with Cu Kα radiation (λ = 0.154060 nm); HighScore Plus 3.0.5 software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Seven coupons per alloy ground to 600 grit and chemically polished 20 min in 10:10:1 water:H2O2:HF; lattice parameters from (111), (200), (220) and (311) peaks plotted vs cos²θ/sinθ and extrapolated to θ = 90°
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the austenite lattice parameter a0 of the 2.5 Al alloy.
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2.5 wt.% Al increases the austenite lattice parameter by 1.41 × 10^-3 nm relative to the base alloy.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), weak-beam dark-field (WBDF) imaging of dissociated dislocations
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Phillips CM12 TEM operating at 120 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: g-3g conditions with (220)-type reflections (sg ≈ 0.22 nm⁻¹); grains with {111} planes nearly aligned with the foil plane selected (minimal dislocation inclination, no 2-D projection correction needed); g·bp analysis confirmed dislocations in the {111} plane
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure partial dislocation separation (d) vs perfect dislocation character angle (α) to calculate the SFE of the 2.5 Al alloy via Eq. (1).
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2.5 Al alloy SFE = 38.3 ± 6.1 mJ m⁻²; Al alloying increases the SFE by 12.0 mJ m⁻² relative to the base alloy.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical SFE calculation from measured partial dislocation separation (Eq. 1)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Isotropic elastic constants G = 74 GPa and ν = 0.3 assumed for each material; the experimental XRD lattice parameter a0 used in the equation
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated SFE of the 2.5 Al alloy (38.3 ± 6.1 mJ m⁻²) derived from measured (d, α) data pairs averaged along several dissociated dislocations.

analytical_models.model_name: SFE from partial dislocation separation and character angle
analytical_models.model_note: Using effective elastic constants (G = 66 GPa, ν = 0.43) instead of isotropic values increased the calculated 2.5 Al SFE by ≈10%; isotropic values were used in the paper.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Newly determined A^LP(Al) = 0.582 [0.289] agrees well with Dyson and Holmes value of 0.56 [0.28]; A^SFE(Al) = 4.9 [2.5] agrees with thermochemical modeling (~5.2) and other reports.

analytical_models.equation_role: Linear empirical relation between austenite composition and lattice parameter
analytical_models.model_note: x_i is wt.% of element i in austenite.

analytical_models.model_name: SFE = Σ A_i^SFE x_i (stacking fault energy)
analytical_models.equation_role: Linear empirical relation between austenite composition and SFE
analytical_models.model_note: x_i is wt.% of element i in austenite.

unmapped_findings: For the 2.5 Al alloy, applying the Williams and Carter correction for partial dislocation strain fields would increase the SFE to 44.0 ± 9.8 mJ m⁻² (uncorrected value 38.3 ± 6.1 mJ m⁻²); the correction was not applied. [b0029]

The Al-induced SFE increase for the 2.5 Al alloy relative to the base alloy is reported as 12.0 mJ m⁻² in the results/discussion (b0029), while the abstract/conclusion give a range of 12–17 mJ m⁻² (b0006, b0034).
Accounting for the partial dislocation strain-field correction yields an estimated A_Al^SFE value of 6.9 mJ m⁻² wt.%⁻¹ in this study, compared with the uncorrected 4.9 mJ m⁻² wt.%⁻¹. [b0033]
The 2.5 Al alloy composition (wt.%) from Table 1: C 0.030, N 0.0034, Ni 15.04, Cr 11.02, Mn 1.08, Si 0.034, Al 2.47; solution annealed at 1060 °C. [b0015]

Ignoring the effect of Al on the austenite lattice parameter can overestimate the calculated austenite C content by δ_C ≈ 0.125–0.176 wt.% (assuming x_Al = 1 wt.%), i.e. on the order of 0.15 wt.% in Al-alloyed AHSS. [b0026, b0034]

Using effective elastic constants for a 12 Ni–12 Cr steel (G = 66 GPa, ν = 0.43) increased the calculated SFE of the 2.5 Al alloy by approximately 10%, but had little effect on the other two alloys. [b0021]
